answer:
Record it as TWO buildings, causally joined by one 1938 event. In CIDOC CRM terms the Combe Farm barn is a new instance of E24 Physical Human-Made Thing, and the barn described in the 1839 tithe survey is a different instance that ceased to exist in 1938 — but the CRM does not make you choose between 'same building' and 'unrelated new build from salvage'. E81 Transformation is the construct for exactly this middle case: it simultaneously ends the old thing and begins the new one, and asserts that the new one preserves recognisable substance and structure from the old.

Why 'new', not 'same'. Two passages of the current specification decide it, and neither depends on the 70% figure.

(1) The E19 Physical Object scope note (crm732#E19) is the movability rule: only instances of E19 can be the target of an E9 Move, and 'If moving requires separating at substantially new boundaries, such as the Temple of Abu Simbel when it was moved, a new instance of E19 Physical Object is created, which incorporates the previous item. The latter process may be documented by the class E81 Transformation.' The barn was not jacked up and carried whole. Its brick plinth walls stayed at Hollow Farm and were built anew at Combe; the frame came apart at its joints; a rotten bay did not travel. Those are substantially new boundaries, so the Abu Simbel rule applies directly.

(2) The E80 Part Removal scope note (crm732#E80) covers the dismantling itself: 'If the instance of E80 Part Removal results in the total decomposition of the original object into pieces, such that the whole ceases to exist, the activity should instead be modelled as an instance of E81 Transformation'. Taking a barn down to its component timbers is total decomposition of the whole.

E24's own scope note (crm732#E24) then licenses the pairing: 'Substantial continuity of the previous matter and structure in the new product can be documented by describing the production process also as an instance of E81 Transformation.' And P123 (crm732#P123) states the consequence for a catalogue: 'New items replace the transformed item or items, which cease to exist as units of documentation.' The 1839 barn is a closed unit of documentation; the 1938 barn is a new one.

What would NOT have been enough. Loss or replacement of fabric alone does not break identity in the CRM — the specification's own identity discussion (crm732#s0065) points out that the Great Sphinx of Giza losing part of its nose leaves it the same monument. A new roof covering, a re-laid plinth and one replaced bay done in situ would have been E11 Modification / E79 Part Addition / E80 Part Removal on a single continuing E24. Likewise a bare change of function would not qualify: under Issue 404 the SIG added a clause to E81 that a 'change in the use of an object' (especially for buildings) does not by itself count as a Transformation. What tips this case is the complete dismantling plus re-founding on new boundaries at a different site.

Proposed record.

B1 'threshing barn, Hollow Farm (early C19)' — E24 Physical Human-Made Thing; P2 has type <threshing barn>; P53 has former or current location <Hollow Farm>; P45 consists of <oak>, <brick>.
B2 'barn at Combe Farm (1938)' — E24 Physical Human-Made Thing; P2 has type <threshing barn>; P53 has former or current location <Combe Farm>; P128 carries INS.
T1938 — E81 Transformation AND E12 Production (multiple instantiation, exactly the pattern of the specification's own example: 'The transformation of the Venetian Loggia in Heraklion into a city hall (E81, E12) resulted in the City Hall of Heraklion'); P124 transformed B1; P123 resulted in B2; P108 has produced B2; P4 has time-span <1938>; P14 carried out by <the estate>; P7 took place at <Combe Farm>; P16 used specific object F; P126 employed <oak>, <brick>, <roof covering material>.
F 'salvaged oak frame of the Hollow Farm barn' — E22 Human-Made Object; B1 P46 is composed of F; B2 P46 is composed of F. This double part-of statement, not the E81 link alone, is what makes the surviving fabric queryable; record the ~70% as P3 has note (or as an E54 Dimension) since the CRM has no proportion-of-original-fabric property.
M1938 — E9 Move; P25 moved F; P27 moved from <Hollow Farm>; P26 moved to <Combe Farm>. The four miles are travelled by the salvaged timbers, which do have their own boundaries and can be moved; they are not travelled by the barn.
D1839 'tithe survey, 1839' — E31 Document; P70 documents B1. This is the practical payoff: the 1839 description attaches to B1 only. The Combe Farm record reaches it through P123/P124, not directly. Putting the tithe description on B2 would be the actual error.
INS — E34 Inscription; P190 has symbolic content 'rebuilt from Hollow Farm barn, 1938'; P67 refers to B1. The plaque is the estate's own assertion of the link and belongs on B2 as evidence, not as the identity statement itself.

Honest caveats. The model is not perfectly self-consistent here: E9 Move still carries 'the relocation of London Bridge from the UK to the USA' as an example (crm732#E9), and London Bridge was likewise dismantled and re-erected — read literally that example treats a dismantled-and-rebuilt structure as one object that moved. The Abu Simbel sentence in E19 is the more specific and more recent rule and I follow it. The underlying question of whether immobile buildings are objects or features has been raised repeatedly without a clean resolution (t0821 in 2015, t1874 in 2025, Issue 716 closed in March 2026 only on paragraph ordering). Martin Doerr's 2015 position in t0821 — 'we should by rule define such a building as new' for any moving of a building — is a proposal in an unresolved thread, not a decision, but it points the same way as the text now in E19. I deliberately type both barns at E24 rather than committing to E22 Human-Made Object or E25 Human-Made Feature, because that is the disputed axis and E24 is where the specification's own building examples (the Colosseum, the Palace of Knossos) sit. If the county survey adopts CRMba, B1 Built Work (a subclass of E24 and E92, covering 'freestanding buildings') is the more precise home for both barns and changes nothing else above.

rejected_alternatives.option: A single E24 continuing from 1839 to today, with E11 Modification for the 1938 work
rejected_alternatives.why_not: E11 is for activities that do not fundamentally change nature or identity (E81's scope note draws exactly this contrast). Here the whole was taken to pieces, so under crm732#E80 the correct construct is E81, not a modification of a surviving whole.

rejected_alternatives.option: E9 Move of the barn itself, with P25/P26/P27
rejected_alternatives.why_not: crm732#E19 restricts E9 Move to instances of E19 Physical Object and states that where moving requires separating at substantially new boundaries — its example is Abu Simbel — a new instance is created instead and the process is documented as E81 Transformation. The plinth stayed behind, so the barn did not move; only the salvaged frame did.

rejected_alternatives.option: E80 Part Removal (dismantling) plus E79 Part Addition (re-erection) on one continuing building
rejected_alternatives.why_not: E80's own scope note (crm732#E80) redirects: total decomposition of the original into pieces such that the whole ceases to exist must be modelled as E81 Transformation. E79/E80 presuppose a whole whose identity survives the operation.

rejected_alternatives.option: E6 Destruction of the 1839 barn plus an independent E12 Production at Combe Farm
rejected_alternatives.why_not: E6 is for things that lose their identity as subjects of documentation, and two unlinked events would throw away the causal and material continuity. E81 is a subclass of both E63 Beginning of Existence and E64 End of Existence, so one event carries both ends and, per crm732#P123, the continuity is expressed by the shared link to it.

rejected_alternatives.option: E22 Human-Made Object for the two barns
rejected_alternatives.why_not: E22 asserts physical boundaries that separate the thing completely and objectively from other objects. A barn bedded on brick plinth walls is precisely the contested case (t0821, t1874, Issue 716), and asserting E22 would also make E9 Move available for the building, which is the reading crm732#E19 rules out. E24 is the honest level. E22 is used here only for the salvaged frame, which genuinely was detached and carried.

rejected_alternatives.option: E25 Human-Made Feature for the two barns
rejected_alternatives.why_not: E25 (via E26) treats the thing as integrally attached to a larger physical thing, i.e. as a feature of the land. The SIG raised this for immobile buildings in t0821 and never settled it, and the specification's building examples sit at E24; committing to E25 would also make the 1938 dismantling harder to state, since the frame demonstrably was separable.

rejected_alternatives.option: E17 Type Assignment / P2 has type change to record the 'rebuilt' status
rejected_alternatives.why_not: E81's scope note distinguishes transformations from re-classifications. Nothing here is a change of what the thing is called; the fabric and the boundaries of the documented unit changed.
E27 comprises pieces of land or sea floor. Hollow Farm and Combe Farm can be recorded as sites or places, but the barn is a human-made thing standing on one, not the site itself.

siblings_considered.why_not: E26 Physical Feature is a sibling subclass of E18 covering things attached in an integral way to a particular physical object. Its subclass E25 is what the SIG floated for immobile buildings in t0821. Typing the barns as features would assert they cannot be documented apart from the ground they stand on — contradicted by the fact that this one was taken down and its frame carried four miles.

E6 Destruction is the other subclass of E64 that could carry the 1938 dismantling. It records loss of identity with no successor, severing the link to the Combe Farm building. E81 does the same ending while also beginning the new thing and, per crm732#P123, expressing the physical continuity between them.

E80 Part Removal is the sibling a reader would reach for to describe taking the barn down. Its own scope note (crm732#E80) sends this case away: when part removal totally decomposes the original such that the whole ceases to exist, model it as E81 Transformation instead.

E25 Human-Made Feature is the sibling for purposely created things attached to a larger object. The salvaged frame was a component with its own pegged-joint boundaries that was in fact detached, carted and re-erected; as an E25 (via E26) it could not be the target of P25 moved, which crm732#E19 reserves for E19 Physical Object.

E11 Modification is the sibling subclass of E7 that covers the dismantling and re-erection work itself, and that work is already carried here by E12/E81. The four-mile carriage of the timbers altered their location and not their form, which is what E9 and only E9 records.

E33 Linguistic Object is the sibling of E31 under E73 and would capture the tithe survey as a text. What the case needs is the survey making a proposition about the barn, which is E31's defining property P70 documents; E33 has no equivalent.

E35 Title is E34's only sibling under E33/E37. 'rebuilt from Hollow Farm barn, 1938' is not a title identifying the building within a cultural convention; it is a text physically applied to the fabric asserting where the fabric came from, which is what E34 covers.

notes:
The decisive sentence — the Abu Simbel rule — lives in the scope note of E19 Physical Object, which is not a class I propose and not a class a search for 'building identity' surfaces. `concept E19` shows only the v7.1.3 scope note, which lacks that paragraph; I only got the current v7.3.2 wording by running `docs ... --json` and reading the full chunk text. The default `docs` preview truncates at ~250 characters, which is shorter than most scope notes, so the paragraph that answers the case was invisible in every ordinary docs result. Suggest showing full chunk text for declaration hits, or at least the paragraph containing the match.

`search.py quote` needs a chunk id and there is no way to see chunk ids without `--json`; `quote "E19 Physical Object" "Abu Simbel"` returned UNKNOWN SOURCE. Printing the chunk_id alongside each docs hit would remove a guessing step.

The thread summary for t0821 was accurate and useful, but the thread itself is a bundle of unrelated 'new CIDOC CRM issue' postings, so the one relevant message (12 of 15) had to be hunted for. Issue 716's register entry says a scope note 'was admitted following the evote on 24 February' but does not reproduce it, and no mailing-list thread cites the issue number, so I could not check whether the v7.4 wording differs from the v7.3.2 text I relied on.

Modelling gaps rather than tool gaps: CRMbase P46 is composed of carries no temporal qualification, so 'the frame was part of B1 and is part of B2' reads atemporally and the chronology has to be recovered from the E81 event; and there is no property for the proportion of original fabric retained, so the 70% has to go in a note or a Dimension. Thanasis Velios makes the related complaint in t1874 that a new identity for what feels like the same thing is counter-intuitive to users — worth warning the county survey's cataloguers about.
